paper.title: Learning to Bid in Contextual First Price Auctions

settings.name_in_paper: Binary feedback with known noise distribution (contextual first price auctions)
unmapped: Repeated contextual first-price auction: bid b_t in [0,1], utility (beta_0(x_t)-b)F(b - alpha_0.x_t)
Competing max bid m_t = alpha_0.x_t + z_t with ||alpha_0||_1 <= W (W known), contexts i.i.d. with ||x_t||_2 <= 1
Noise distribution F known, log-concave density with bounds B_1 <= f <= B_2, f' <= B_3 on [-W,1+W]
Learner knows its own valuation function beta_0
Binary feedback: only win indicator 1{b_t >= m_t} observed
settings.definition_quote: Binary feedback: the learner only observes the indicator $\delta_t = \1\{b_t \geq m_t\}$. ... In this section, we assume the learner knows the noise distribution $\F$, i.e., $f$ and $F$ are known.

settings.name_in_paper: Binary feedback with partially-known noise distribution
unmapped: Contextual first-price auction bidding with linear competing bid model
Noise = known base distribution F_0 scaled by unknown sigma, |1/sigma| <= W
Bids restricted to be >= a minimum Delta; benchmark truncated at Delta
Eigenvalue assumptions on Sigma = E[x x^T] (Assumption 3.1)
settings.definition_quote: we extend to the case that the noise distribution $\F$ is parameterized by a zero-mean base noise distribution $\F_0$ and a variance $\sigma^2 (\sigma > 0)$, where $\F_{0}$ is known (e.g. $\mathcal{N}(0, 1)$) but $\sigma$ is unknown.

settings.name_in_paper: Full information feedback model with unknown noise distribution
unmapped: Contextual first-price auction bidding; learner observes the competing max bid m_t after each round
Unknown log-concave noise distribution; learner knows bound B_2 on density
Minimum eigenvalue of Sigma bounded below
settings.definition_quote: In this section, we consider the full information feedback model with unknown noise distribution, i.e., the learner has no information of noise distribution, however she can always observe the highest bid of all other bidders $m_t$.

settings.name_in_paper: Full information feedback with known Gaussian noise (lower bound)
unmapped: Contextual first-price auction bidding; z_t ~ N(0, sigma^2) with known sigma; m_t observed
settings.definition_quote: we show the lower bound of regret for the full information feedback model with known noise distribution, i.e. $\F$ is known and $m_t$ is always realized at the end of each time $t$.

algorithms.name: Episodic MLE bidding algorithm (binary feedback, known noise) (Algorithm 1)
Episodic MLE bidding algorithm (binary feedback, partially known noise) (Algorithm 2)
Episodic log-concave density estimation + MLE bidding algorithm (full information, unknown noise) (Algorithm 3)

conditions: Assumption 2.2: noise density differentiable and log-concave
Assumption 2.3: B_1 <= f <= B_2 and f' <= B_3 on [-W,1+W]

source.label: thm:binary-known-noise-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumption~\ref{assump:bounded-noise} and Assumption~\ref{assump:log-concave} hold, setting $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret achieved in the binary feedback model with known noise distribution is at most $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ omits $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Õ hides log log T and constants depending on W, B_2, B_3. Regret defined with expectations but stated with prob 1-delta; recorded as high-probability. Comparator is the clairvoyant optimal per-context bid. MLE is convex so polynomial time.

conditions: Assumption 3.1: eigenvalues of Sigma=E[x x^T] in [lambda_2, lambda_1], Sigma - E[x]E[x]^T > lambda_3 I
Bids and benchmark truncated below at Delta > 0

source.label: thm:regret-binary-partial-known-noise
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assump:log-concave},~\ref{assump:bounded-noise} and~\ref{assump:eigenvalue-ub} hold, setting $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret (w.r.t the benchmark defined in Eq.~(\ref{eq:opt-bid-binary-partial-known-noise})) achieved in the binary feedback model with partially known noise distribution is bounded by $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ ignores $\log T$ and $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Benchmark is optimal bid truncated at minimum bid Delta (not the gap). Õ hides log T, log log T.

conditions: Assumption 3.1 (only minimum eigenvalue of Sigma >= lambda_2 needed)

source.label: thm:full-info-regret
source.quote: Suppose Assumptions~\ref{assump:log-concave},~\ref{assump:bounded-noise}, and~\ref{assump:eigenvalue-ub} hold, and $T$ is sufficiently large. Given $T_s = T^{1-2^{-s}}, s = 1,2,\cdots,$ then with probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret is bounded by $R(T) \leq \widetilde{O}\left(\sqrt{d\log(d/\delta) T}\right)$, where $\widetilde{O}$ ignores $\log T$ and $\log\log T$ terms.

results.notes: Paper leaves computational efficiency as future work.

conditions: Restricted to bidding policies in Pi: b_t = max{0, alpha_t.x_t + phi^{-1}(beta_0(x_t) - alpha_t.x_t)} with alpha_t H_{t-1}-measurable and ||alpha_t||_1 <= W
z_t ~ N(0, sigma^2) with sigma known
contexts with coordinates i.i.d. uniform on {-1,1} (in proof)

source.label: thm:lower-bound-known-F
source.quote: For any $T$, we assume that the market value $z_t, 1 \leq t \leq T$ are fully observed. We further assume $z_t \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2)$, where $\sigma$ is known. Let $\Pi$ be the set of bidding polices $\pi$ defined in Eq.~(\ref{eq:bidding-policy}), then any bidding policy $\pi$ must incur expected regret $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected utilities, so pseudo-regret. Proof concludes Omega(sqrt(T log T)) but theorem states Omega(sqrt T).
